fullPassage: The idea that our senses may be deceiving us was taken up by the French philosopher and mathematician René Descartes. He realized that sometimes our senses give us a false impression — a straight stick in a glass of water appears to be bent, for example. And if we know that they can be unreliable, it would be wrong to trust them completely — everything that we experience with our senses might be false. It might even be that we are asleep, and that the world we are experiencing is no more than a dream, or that God or some mischievous power is making us believe things that are not really true. If that is the case, though, we can never know anything for sure. But Descartes then showed that there was one thing he could be sure of: In order to be deceived, he must exist, and exist as a thing that thinks. So, although his senses could not be trusted, he could be sure he existed as something that was capable of thinking and reasoning.

questions.passage: The idea that our senses may be ①<u>deceiving</u> us was taken up by the French philosopher and mathematician René Descartes. He ②<u>realized</u> that sometimes our senses give us a false impression — a straight stick in a glass of water appears to be bent, for example. And if we know that they can be unreliable, it would be wrong ③<u>to trust</u> them completely — everything that we experience with our senses might be false. It might even be that we are asleep, and that the world we are experiencing is no more than a dream, or that God or some mischievous power is making us ④<u>to believe</u> things that are not really true. If that is the case, though, we can never know ⑤<u>anything</u> for sure.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ to believe → believe: make + 목적어 + 동사원형 (사역동사 구문). to부정사가 아닌 원형부정사가 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
❌④to believe: make(사역동사) + us(목적어) + believe(원형부정사)
✅①deceiving: may be + ~ing(진행형)
✅②realized: 과거시제
✅③to trust: it would be wrong + to V
✅⑤anything: never + anything(부정어+any)
det.tip: make + 목적어 + 원형부정사 (사역동사 구문)

questions.passage: The idea that our senses may be deceiving us was ①<u>taken</u> up by the French philosopher and mathematician René Descartes. He realized that sometimes our senses ②<u>give</u> us a false impression — a straight stick in a glass of water appears ③<u>to be bent</u>, for example. And if we know that they can be unreliable, it would be wrong to trust them completely — everything ④<u>what</u> we experience with our senses might be false. It might even be that we are asleep, and that the world we are ⑤<u>experiencing</u> is no more than a dream.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ what → that: everything 뒤에는 관계대명사 that이 와야 한다. what은 선행사를 포함하므로 everything과 함께 쓸 수 없다.
det.analysis:
❌④what: everything(선행사) + that(관계대명사) → what은 선행사 포함이므로 불가
✅①taken: was taken up(수동태)
✅②give: our senses(복수주어) + give
✅③to be bent: appears + to V
✅⑤experiencing: are experiencing(진행형)
det.tip: everything/anything/nothing + that (O) / everything + what (X)
